clue.text: Order toast and get no end of it

indicators.note: having no end means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to char is to scorch or toast
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone asks for toast and is told they will not get any of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' simply refers back to the word get, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to command or instruct them to do it.

clue.text: Heads of coven secretly do plan evil, bitter spell

indicators.note: evil suggests something corrupted and twisted out of shape, so the letters are reworked
heads are the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letters of two words
taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: Witches secretly plotting a wicked, bitter spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell suggests witchcraft after the coven; here it is a period of weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief spell of sudden very cold weather, bitter in the sense of freezing.

clue.text: Animal's inclination to toss head and run away

indicators.note: tossing away the head means losing the first letter

parts.note: a cant is a slope or tilt
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: An animal tends to toss its head and bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Inclination reads as a tendency, but here it is a physical slant.
explanation.definitionFit: The antelope is a swift, horned grazing mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Good assortment of art (mostly) I'll see here?

definitions.text: Good assortment of art (mostly) I'll see here?

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed selection, so the letters are jumbled
mostly means not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: A visitor expects to see a fine range of art here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a place where one sees a good assortment of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleries are rooms or buildings where collections of paintings and sculpture are displayed to the public.

clue.text: Famous ostrich I trained

indicators.note: something trained has been shaped and drilled into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the bird plus the pronoun

explanation.surface: A celebrity ostrich that I personally trained.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic event or place is notable and celebrated, significant enough to be remembered by later generations.

clue.text: Mind telling niece off?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: Would you mind telling your niece off?
explanation.walkthrough: Mind looks like the verb in a polite request; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence is the capacity to think and reason, the faculty of the brain.

clue.text: Truths half-hidden by politician? This could create a stink

indicators.note: with half hidden only the first half of the word shows

parts.note: the first three of six letters
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician hiding half the truth could cause a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to trump is to break wind; the surface also nods at a certain American politician.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for breaking wind, which does indeed create a smell.

clue.text: African country's uprising checking over district

indicators.note: rising up in a down entry means the word reads from bottom to top
checking means holding back or restraining, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An uprising in an African country being put down across a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or zone, a territorial division like a district.

clue.text: Unite after revolutionary gives ground

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
to wed is to unite in marriage

explanation.surface: A trade union leader backs down after a revolutionary takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the uniting word second. Gives ground looks like a phrase meaning retreats; ground is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Food ground between the teeth has been masticated, the past tense of grinding with the jaws.

clue.text: Recently allowed back in bed

indicators.note: placed in means set inside another word

parts.note: to lay someone is a slang way to bed them

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone has lately been permitted back into bed, perhaps after a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something happening in the recent past, not long ago.

clue.text: Rugs get woven — around 50 fray

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the Roman numeral, holding it inside
threads that are woven are interlaced in a new pattern, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written for mixing
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Woven rugs tend to fray at the edges, perhaps around fifty of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a fight or brawl, and a struggle is a physical contest or tussle.

clue.text: Stood up distressed when caught

indicators.note: caught here means picked up by the ear, as in catching what someone says

parts.note: straitened means in distressed or difficult circumstances

explanation.surface: Someone was jilted on a date and upset when found out.
explanation.walkthrough: Stood up suggests jilted; it means made upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stood up has been set upright or vertical, made straight.

clue.text: Clear up wine after a change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart means the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: Soave is a dry white Italian wine

explanation.surface: A hangover cured by wine after someone changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter A of the wine is replaced by L; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a mystery or puzzle is to work out its answer, find the explanation.

clue.text: Call box almost unreal!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, shortened to tele
phoney means fake or unreal

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a telephone box that seems too unlikely to be real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call box' looks like one phrase, a phone booth, but call is the definition and box the television.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone is to ring or phone them, so the verb matches.

clue.text: Post letter?

parts.note: surface reading: a letter to be sent in the mail
setter's reading: a letter written to apply for a job, a post

explanation.walkthrough: Post looks like the mail service; here it is a position of employment, and the letter asks for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A job application is a formal written request for a position, often sent as a letter.

clue.text: Nudist removing bottom half in front of gathering, as might be expected

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom half is the second half of the word, which is dropped

parts.note: a naturist is a nudist
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: A nudist showing their bottom half at a rally, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' puts the trimmed word first.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally means of course, in the way one would predict.

clue.text: One's pressed for a face-to-face meeting

definitions.text: One's pressed for a face-to-face meeting

parts.words: One's pressed for a face-to-face meeting
parts.note: surface reading: a busy person urged to meet someone in person

parts.words: One's pressed for a face-to-face meeting
parts.note: setter's reading: a button pushed at the front door so the resident comes out to meet you

explanation.walkthrough: Pressed looks like rushed or urged; here it is physically pushed with a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor pushes this button at a house entrance to summon someone and meet them in person.

clue.text: Individual one harshly criticised, without love

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lone person, harshly criticised and without love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside, so the criticism surrounds love.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolated case stands alone, single and separate, an individual instance.

clue.text: Gussets go in pants, creating whiffs

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, signalling the letters are a mess to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: Underwear gussets are sewn into trousers, causing bad smells.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like underwear and whiffs like smells, both lavatorial misdirection; a whiff here is a faint hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiff of something is a slight trace or hint, just as a suggestion is.

clue.text: Effective American fuel raising energy

parts.note: US is short for American

indicators.note: in a down entry raising moves the energy letter higher, earlier in the word, rearranging it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: American fuel that is efficient at boosting energy.
explanation.walkthrough: E for energy moves up from third to first place in the fuel word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effective does its job well, which is to say serviceable and practical.

clue.text: Where camper might be fixed

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: inside canvas shelter
second meaning: firmly set on a purpose

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer says where a camper sleeps; as one word it means determined.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed stare or a mind set on something is concentrated and determined.

clue.text: Fake article possessed by Nitsy upset Conservative

indicators.note: possessed by means held within, so the article sits inside
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the setter's name is rearranged

parts.note: the setter's own pseudonym, taken as written
the definite article
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A fake article in a newspaper upsets the setter, a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic materials are artificial, man-made imitations rather than genuine natural ones.

clue.text: Regularly visit hospital with relative

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone who often visits a relative in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to frequent it habitually, like a ghost that keeps returning.

clue.text: Country's two rivers

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A nation that boasts two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation, but it is the adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Country as an adjective describes the countryside, away from towns, which is the meaning of rural.

clue.text: Worry about heartless queen's visit

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to fret is to worry

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its middle letter

explanation.surface: Anxiety over a cold-hearted monarch's state visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to go there often, to visit it habitually.

clue.text: Easy to get hospital department to follow infection

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a common infection
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Being admitted to a hospital department is simple once you have caught an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' tells you the department goes after the infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent speech or movement flows smoothly and effortlessly, which is to say easy.

clue.text: Freedom to celebrate catching birdie by its tail

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, like a net

parts.note: to laud is to praise or celebrate
a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its tail: the same small word read again, keeping only its final letter

explanation.surface: Free to celebrate after grabbing a small bird by the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is scope or leeway to act as one chooses, a kind of freedom.

clue.text: Shutter that's closed at night?

parts.note: surface reading: a window shutter closed when it gets dark
setter's reading: the fold of skin that shuts over the eye when we sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Shutter suggests a window, but the thing shut at night is part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin covering the eye shuts like a blind when sleeping.
